title: Machine-learning selection identifies a six-metabolite signature for one-year cardiovascular events after PCI in type 2 diabetes
summary: VSURF feature selection prioritized six serum metabolites—ADPR, 1-methylnicotinamide, D-ribose 5-phosphate, nicotinamide, L-tryptophan and phosphatidylcholine PC(36:2)—for one-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) after PCI in patients with type 2 diabetes. Random-forest and XGBoost models were tested in a nested case-control study and an independent prospective cohort of 301 patients; in the external cohort, reported AUCs were 0.92 and 0.94 for MACEs, respectively. The study also linked NAD+ biosynthesis perturbation to altered bioenergetics, inflammation and proliferation in high-glucose-cultured human aortic smooth-muscle cells.
ai_technology: VSURF random-forest variable selection; random forest and XGBoost classifiers
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University; Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University

evidence.tested: Random-forest and XGBoost models were tested in a nested case-control study and an independent prospective cohort of 301 patients; in the external cohort, reported AUCs were 0.92 and 0.94 for MACEs, respectively.
evidence.unknown: The discovery component was a matched nested case-control sample (108 cases and 108 controls) from a single center; external validation was in a separate Chinese cohort of 301 patients, so transportability to other populations is unknown. AUCs describe retrospective/prospective cohort validation, not demonstrated clinical utility or improved patient outcomes. HASMC experiments do not prove the metabolites cause clinical events, and the paper states further mechanistic work is needed.
evidence.ai_role: VSURF selected a six-metabolite feature set from serum metabolomic profiles. Random-forest and XGBoost models used that panel to predict one-year post-PCI outcomes; targeted metabolite testing evaluated the panel in a separate prospective cohort.
